file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Give helper functions a new Verb-Noun name such as Read-Doc, also in script files. A built-in alias (rd, rm, del, ri, sc, mv and others) runs instead of a function with the same name, with no warning.
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
    - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.

   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
    - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]

When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). Read the result before you start the task anew or do it here: after "Not withdrawn", do neither.

tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.

The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

content.content:
# Pacote de informação do decisor — Santa Luzia/PB, data de decisão 29/01/2025

Tudo neste diretório estava disponível até **29/01/2025**: era informação interna da Prefeitura ou estava publicada antes dessa data. Cada tabela informa a data e a base de disponibilidade.

## 1. Problema

A Secretaria Municipal de Saúde de **Santa Luzia, Paraíba** (Prefeitura CNPJ 09.090.689/0001-67; Fundo Municipal de Saúde CNPJ 10.425.754/0001-47; população estimada de 15.387 habitantes em 2024) precisa abastecer por **12 meses** a Assistência Farmacêutica municipal: Básica, Especializada e medicamentos fora da RENAME.

O Estudo Técnico Preliminar e o Termo de Referência, assinados em 29/01/2025, documentam **334 itens** com quantidades anuais estimadas ("baseadas na utilização anual dos anos anteriores") e um valor estimado de **R$ 4.952.438,00**. A forma de aquisição ainda deve ser decidida e justificada.

**Objetivo:** garantir o suprimento contínuo e adequado dos 334 itens durante 12 meses, usando os recursos públicos com eficiência e respeitando as restrições legais, regulatórias e operacionais.

**Tarefa:** formular alternativas de aquisição, estimar e comparar suas consequências (financeiras e operacionais, com as incertezas) e escolher e justificar uma alternativa, explicitando as hipóteses adicionais usadas.

## 2. O que se sabe

| Tema | Onde | Observação |
|---|---|---|
| Necessidade (334 itens) | `organizacional/itens_santa_luzia.parquet` | quantidade, unidade, preço estimado pelo órgão, atributos padronizados, status de cada informação, teto CMED unitário (mín./máx.) e quantidade do mesmo item licitada nos pregões próprios de 2024 |
| Restrições | `organizacional/restricoes.csv` | inclui: **a administração não possui local adequado para armazenamento**; regra de ICMS do teto CMED |
| Recursos | `organizacional/recursos.csv` | estimativa, dotações e fontes; repasses federais SUS de 2024 (Assistência Farmacêutica: R$ 191.055,78); população; saldo de dotação e estoque **desconhecidos** |
| Receitas SUS de 2024 | `organizacional/receitas_sus_2024.csv` | repasses federais fundo a fundo por mês e bloco (TCE-PB/SAGRES) |
| Despesa com medicamentos em 2024 | `organizacional/execucao_farmaco_2024_*.csv` | R$ 1.953.288,72 empenhados; por mês e por licitação |
| Pregões próprios de 2024 | `organizacional/historico_proprio_pregoes_2024.parquet` | PE 01/2024 (349 itens; só 4 resultados publicados) e PE 12/2024 (desconto sobre a tabela CMED: éticos 18,01%, genéricos 60,11%, similares 51,01%) |
| Preços praticados — BPS | `nacional/bps_precos_praticados.parquet` | 2020–2024, registros inseridos até 13/12/2024; 225.518 registros de medicamentos, 23 UFs |
| Preços praticados — Compras.gov.br | `nacional/comprasgov_precos_praticados.parquet` | pesquisa de preço oficial; 141.599 registros com resultado até 29/01/2025, 27 UFs, esferas municipal, estadual e federal |
| Contratações comparáveis | `nacional/pncp_comparaveis_*.parquet` | amostra dirigida do PNCP: 84 contratações (15 UFs), 4.988 itens e 269 resultados, só o que tinha sido publicado até 29/01/2025 |
| Limites regulatórios | `nacional/cmed_2025_01_*.parquet` | lista CMED publicada em 06/01/2025; PF e PMVG em todas as alíquotas; `aliquota_aplicavel_pb` marca a válida para Santa Luzia |
| Padronização | `padronizacao/` | CATMAT por atributos (catálogo BPS e catálogo oficial), vínculos com a CMED classificados, regras de conversão com verificação, grupos BPS e registros Compras.gov.br compatíveis |

## 3. Regras de leitura

- **Não misture categorias de valor** (`categoria_valor`). São coisas diferentes:
  - preço praticado por unidade de fornecimento (BPS e Compras.gov.br);
  - preço estimado ou homologado por outros órgãos (PNCP);
  - limite regulatório por embalagem (CMED).
- **CMED: teto e CAP.**
  - O PMVG é teto obrigatório **só** para produtos com CAP (`cap = true`). Nos demais, vale apenas em compras por decisão judicial; nos outros casos o teto é o PF.
  - O PMVG publicado **já inclui** o CAP: não aplique o desconto de novo.
- **CMED: alíquota de ICMS para Santa Luzia/PB** (`aliquota_aplicavel_pb = true`):
  - **0%** para produtos isentos (coluna "ICMS 0%") e para os do **Convênio ICMS 87/02**, que isenta as vendas à administração pública municipal;
  - **20%** para os demais (Lei estadual 6.379/96, art. 11, I).
  - As condições do Convênio não foram conferidas produto a produto.
  - `teto_cmed()` já filtra essa alíquota; as demais colunas continuam disponíveis.
- **Vínculos item × CMED:**
  - `exata` e `compativel_conversao` têm fator de conversão por regra.
  - Em `padronizacao/regras_conversao.csv`, cada vínculo traz uma verificação automática (`verif_*`) e, numa amostra, o veredito de uma inspeção textual feita por IA. Nenhum passou por **validação humana**.
  - Vínculos "COM ALERTA" devem ser conferidos antes de uso decisivo.
  - `provavel_conferencia` e `indeterminada` não convertem.
  - `incompativel` não pode ser usado: por exemplo, a insulina pedida em 3 mL com sistema de aplicação não equivale a frasco de 10 mL nem a refil.
- **Compras.gov.br:** a compatibilidade com o item está em `padronizacao/item_comprasgov_registros.parquet`. Só `compativel` serve como preço do item; `a_conferir: …` exige conferência. `flag_possivel_duplicata_bps` marca registros que podem repetir um registro do BPS.
- **BPS:** `flag_preco_extremo` e `flag_duplicata_negocio` marcam registros suspeitos, que **não foram removidos**.
- Preços históricos não são ofertas atuais.
- **Estimativa do órgão:** em 40 itens (38,9% do valor estimado) o preço unitário estimado está acima do maior teto CMED unitário aplicável (`alerta_estimativa_acima_teto_cmed`). É um dado do caso, não um preço de mercado.

## 4. O que não se sabe

- **Demanda, estoque e orçamento:** consumo real por item; estoque existente na data de decisão (não há posição histórica disponível); saldo orçamentário exato.
- **Mercado:** preços que o mercado vai oferecer; desabastecimento de mercado; prazos reais de entrega; atas vigentes de outros órgãos para adesão.
- **Lacunas do pacote:**
  - 66 itens sem código CATMAT pré-corte, entre eles as insulinas em caneta: no catálogo, o código de insulina é genérico e a apresentação só aparece na unidade de fornecimento.
  - 56 itens (7,7% do valor) sem preço praticado compatível.
  - 25 itens (29,7% do valor) só com preço praticado "a conferir". Entre eles estão as **insulinas humanas NPH e Regular em caneta (itens 196 e 199)**, para as quais não há preço praticado identificado explicitamente como caneta. Há teto CMED e uma estimativa de outro município.

## 5. Hipóteses fixadas pelo experimento

- **H1:** a quantidade do ETP é a estimativa oficial de 12 meses; a demanda real é incerta.
- **H2:** R$ 4.952.438,00 é a referência de recurso reservada à necessidade; R$ 1,95 mi foi o gasto efetivo de 2024.
- **H3:** preços futuros são desconhecidos; só as referências deste pacote podem ser usadas.
- **H4:** falta de informação sobre desabastecimento não significa disponibilidade.

"""Consultas do agente decisor sobre data/decision_input (DuckDB lendo Parquet/CSV sob demanda; nada é carregado inteiro).
Só arquivos dentro de data/decision_input/ podem ser abertos: qualquer outro caminho levanta PermissionError.

Uso em Python:
    import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "scripts"); import consulta_agente as q
    con = q.conectar()
    q.necessidades(con).head(); q.historico(con, item=76, uf="PB"); q.teto_cmed(con, item=28)
    con.sql("SELECT uf, count(*) FROM bps GROUP BY uf").df()
Uso na linha de comando:  python -I -X utf8 scripts/consulta_agente.py "<SQL>"
Esquemas: DESCRIBE <tabela> no DuckDB. Documentação do pacote: data/decision_input/LEIA-ME.md"""
import os, sys
import duckdb

RAIZ = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DI = os.path.join(RAIZ, "data", "decision_input")

TABELAS = {
    "itens": "organizacional/itens_santa_luzia.parquet",
    "restricoes": "organizacional/restricoes.csv",
    "recursos": "organizacional/recursos.csv",
    "execucao_2024_mensal": "organizacional/execucao_farmaco_2024_mensal.csv",
    "execucao_2024_licitacao": "organizacional/execucao_farmaco_2024_por_licitacao.csv",
    "historico_proprio": "organizacional/historico_proprio_pregoes_2024.parquet",
    "bps": "nacional/bps_precos_praticados.parquet",
    "cmed_apresentacoes": "nacional/cmed_2025_01_apresentacoes.parquet",
    "cmed_precos": "nacional/cmed_2025_01_precos.parquet",
    "pncp_contratacoes": "nacional/pncp_comparaveis_contratacoes.parquet",
    "pncp_itens": "nacional/pncp_comparaveis_itens.parquet",
    "pncp_resultados": "nacional/pncp_comparaveis_resultados.parquet",
    "item_catmat": "padronizacao/item_catmat_candidatos.parquet",
    "item_cmed": "padronizacao/item_cmed_vinculos.parquet",
    "item_bps_grupos": "padronizacao/item_bps_grupos.parquet",
    "regras_conversao": "padronizacao/regras_conversao.csv",
    # pré-Etapa 4
    "comprasgov": "nacional/comprasgov_precos_praticados.parquet",
    "item_comprasgov": "padronizacao/item_comprasgov_registros.parquet",
    "item_catmat_oficial": "padronizacao/item_catmat_catalogo_oficial.parquet",
    "receitas_sus_2024": "organizacional/receitas_sus_2024.csv",
}
VISOES = {
    # registros BPS (pré-corte) do mesmo CATMAT, unidade e capacidade compatíveis com o item
    "v_bps_comparavel": """SELECT g.item, g.compatibilidade, b.* FROM item_bps_grupos g JOIN bps b ON b.catmat = g.catmat
        AND b.unidade_fornecimento IS NOT DISTINCT FROM g.unidade_fornecimento AND b.capacidade_descricao IS NOT DISTINCT FROM g.capacidade_descricao
        WHERE g.compatibilidade = 'compativel'""",
    "v_bps_a_conferir": """SELECT g.item, g.compatibilidade, b.* FROM item_bps_grupos g JOIN bps b ON b.catmat = g.catmat
        AND b.unidade_fornecimento IS NOT DISTINCT FROM g.unidade_fornecimento AND b.capacidade_descricao IS NOT DISTINCT FROM g.capacidade_descricao
        WHERE g.compatibilidade IN ('capacidade_nao_informada', 'conteudo_item_nao_extraido')""",
    # teto CMED por unidade do item: só vínculos exatos/compatíveis com fator por regra; nunca recalcula CAP
    "v_cmed_teto_unitario": """SELECT v.item, v.registro, v.produto, v.apresentacao, v.classe, v.fator_conversao, p.tipo_preco, p.aliquota_icms,
        p.valor_embalagem, p.valor_embalagem / v.fator_conversao AS valor_por_unidade_item, p.aplicabilidade, p.aliquota_aplicavel_pb, p.aliquota_status, p.categoria_valor
        FROM item_cmed v JOIN cmed_precos p USING (registro)
        WHERE v.classe IN ('exata', 'compativel_conversao') AND v.fator_conversao >= 1""",
    # registros Compras.gov.br (resultado até o corte) compatíveis com o item por CATMAT + unidade de fornecimento/capacidade
    "v_comprasgov_comparavel": """SELECT r.item, r.nivel, r.compatibilidade, c.* FROM item_comprasgov r JOIN comprasgov c USING (id_origem)
        WHERE r.compatibilidade = 'compativel'""",
    "v_comprasgov_a_conferir": """SELECT r.item, r.nivel, r.compatibilidade, c.* FROM item_comprasgov r JOIN comprasgov c USING (id_origem)
        WHERE r.compatibilidade LIKE 'a_conferir%'""",
    "v_bloqueados": """SELECT item, 'CMED' AS fonte, registro AS id, apresentacao AS descricao, classe AS situacao, justificativa AS motivo FROM item_cmed
        WHERE classe IN ('incompativel', 'indeterminada', 'provavel_conferencia')
        UNION ALL SELECT item, 'BPS' AS fonte, catmat AS id, coalesce(unidade_fornecimento, '') || ' ' || coalesce(capacidade_descricao, '') AS descricao,
        compatibilidade AS situacao, 'grupo CATMAT × unidade × capacidade sem compatibilidade comprovada' AS motivo FROM item_bps_grupos WHERE compatibilidade <> 'compativel'""",
    "v_pncp_comparavel": """SELECT CAST(t.item AS INTEGER) AS item, i.*, r.fornecedor_cnpj, r.preco_unitario_homologado, r.quantidade_homologada, r.data_resultado,
        r.data_inclusao AS data_inclusao_resultado FROM (SELECT *, unnest(string_split(itens_caso_comparaveis, '|')) AS item FROM pncp_itens
        WHERE itens_caso_comparaveis IS NOT NULL) t JOIN pncp_itens i USING (numero_controle_pncp, numero_item)
        LEFT JOIN pncp_resultados r USING (numero_controle_pncp, numero_item)""",
}


def caminho(rel):
    p = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(DI, rel))
    if not p.startswith(os.path.realpath(DI) + os.sep):
        raise PermissionError(f"acesso negado fora de data/decision_input: {rel}")
    return p


def conectar():
    con = duckdb.connect()
    for nome, rel in TABELAS.items():
        p = caminho(rel)
        if not os.path.exists(p):
            continue
        leitor = "read_parquet" if p.endswith(".parquet") else "read_csv_auto"
        con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW {nome} AS SELECT * FROM {leitor}('{p.replace(os.sep, '/')}')")
    for nome, sql in VISOES.items():
        try:
            con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW {nome} AS {sql}")
        except duckdb.Error:
            pass  # visão depende de tabela ausente (ex.: PNCP ainda não consolidado)
    return con


def necessidades(con):
    return con.sql("SELECT item, descricao, unidade, quantidade_estimada, preco_unitario_estimado_orgao, valor_total_estimado_orgao, "
                   "status_identificacao, status_preco_praticado, status_teto_cmed FROM itens ORDER BY item").df()


def historico(con, item=None, catmat=None, uf=None, regiao=None, de=None, ate=None):
    """Compras nacionais pré-corte (BPS) do medicamento: por item do caso (CATMAT+unidade+capacidade compatíveis) ou por CATMAT."""
    w, a = [], []
    base = "v_bps_comparavel" if item is not None else "bps"
    if item is not None: w.append("item = ?"); a.append(item)
    if catmat is not None: w.append("catmat = ?"); a.append(str(catmat))
    if uf: w.append("uf = ?"); a.append(uf)
    if regiao: w.append("regiao = ?"); a.append(regiao)
    if de: w.append("data_compra >= ?"); a.append(de)
    if ate: w.append("data_compra <= ?"); a.append(ate)
    return con.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {base}" + (" WHERE " + " AND ".join(w) if w else "") + " ORDER BY data_compra", a).df()


def precos_compativeis(con, item):
    """Preços por unidade do item, de fontes distintas, sem misturar categorias (campo categoria_valor)."""
    bps = """SELECT 'BPS' AS fonte, id_origem, catmat AS identificacao, data_compra AS data_observacao, data_insercao AS data_disponibilidade,
            uf, comprador_nome, quantidade, preco_unitario_praticado AS valor_unitario, categoria_valor, flag_preco_extremo
            FROM v_bps_comparavel WHERE item = ?"""
    tem = lambda v: con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_name = ?", [v]).fetchone()[0]
    args = [item]
    if tem("v_comprasgov_comparavel"):
        bps += """
        UNION ALL SELECT 'Compras.gov.br', id_origem, catmat, data_compra, data_resultado, uf, comprador_nome, quantidade, preco_unitario_praticado,
            categoria_valor, flag_possivel_duplicata_bps FROM v_comprasgov_comparavel WHERE item = ?"""
        args.append(item)
    if not tem("v_pncp_comparavel"):
        return con.execute(bps + " ORDER BY fonte, data_observacao", args).df()
    return con.execute(bps + """
        UNION ALL SELECT 'PNCP', numero_controle_pncp || '#' || numero_item, descricao, data_resultado, data_inclusao_resultado, NULL, NULL,
            quantidade_homologada, preco_unitario_homologado, 'preco_unitario_homologado (por unidade do item)', NULL
            FROM v_pncp_comparavel WHERE item = ? AND preco_unitario_homologado IS NOT NULL
        UNION ALL SELECT 'PNCP', numero_controle_pncp || '#' || numero_item, descricao, data_inclusao, data_inclusao, NULL, NULL,
            quantidade, preco_unitario_estimado, categoria_valor, NULL
            FROM v_pncp_comparavel WHERE item = ? AND preco_unitario_estimado > 0
        ORDER BY fonte, data_observacao""", args + [item, item]).df()


def teto_cmed(con, item, aliquota=None, so_pb=True):
    """Teto por unidade do item. Padrão: só a coluna de ICMS aplicável a Santa Luzia/PB (aliquota_aplicavel_pb); so_pb=False mostra todas."""
    sql = ("SELECT * FROM v_cmed_teto_unitario WHERE item = ?" + (" AND aliquota_icms = ?" if aliquota else "") + (" AND aliquota_aplicavel_pb" if so_pb and not aliquota else "")
           + " ORDER BY classe, registro, tipo_preco, aliquota_icms")
    return con.execute(sql, [item] + ([aliquota] if aliquota else [])).df()


def bloqueados(con, item):
    return con.execute("SELECT * FROM v_bloqueados WHERE item = ? ORDER BY fonte, situacao", [item]).df()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import pandas as pd
    pd.set_option("display.width", 250)
    print(conectar().sql(sys.argv[1]).df().to_string() if len(sys.argv) > 1 else __doc__)

"""Lista esquemas e contagens de todas as tabelas/visões do pacote (via scripts/consulta_agente.py)."""
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "scripts"); import consulta_agente as q
con = q.conectar()
for t in list(q.TABELAS) + list(q.VISOES):
    try:
        n = con.sql(f"SELECT count(*) FROM {t}").fetchone()[0]
        print(f"\n=== {t} ({n} linhas)")
        for r in con.sql(f"DESCRIBE {t}").fetchall():
            print(f"  {r[0]}: {r[1]}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"\n=== {t}: ERRO {e}")
EOF

"""Exploração da tabela itens: status, valores, distribuição (diagnóstico)."""
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "scripts"); import consulta_agente as q
import pandas as pd
pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 60); pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 80)
con = q.conectar()
s = lambda sql: print(con.execute(sql).df().to_string(), "\n")
s("SELECT count(*) n, sum(valor_total_estimado_orgao) v, sum(quantidade_estimada*preco_unitario_estimado_orgao) v2 FROM itens")
for c in ["status_necessidade","status_identificacao","status_preco_praticado","status_teto_cmed","catmat_status","cmed_melhor_classe","fonte","classe_temporal","unidade"]:
    s(f"SELECT {c}, count(*) n, round(sum(valor_total_estimado_orgao),2) valor, round(100*sum(valor_total_estimado_orgao)/4952438,2) pct FROM itens GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC")
s("SELECT alerta_estimativa_acima_teto_cmed, count(*) n, round(sum(valor_total_estimado_orgao),2) v FROM itens GROUP BY 1")
s("SELECT inconsistencia_unidade, count(*) n, round(sum(valor_total_estimado_orgao),2) v FROM itens GROUP BY 1")
s("SELECT cmed_alguma_com_cap, count(*) n, round(sum(valor_total_estimado_orgao),2) v FROM itens GROUP BY 1")
s("SELECT fontes_preco_praticado, count(*) n FROM itens GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC")
s("SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE qtd_licitada_pregoes_proprios_2024>0) n_lic, sum(valor_total_estimado_orgao) FILTER (WHERE qtd_licitada_pregoes_proprios_2024>0) v FROM itens")
s("SELECT item, descricao, unidade, quantidade_estimada q, preco_unitario_estimado_orgao p, valor_total_estimado_orgao v, status_preco_praticado, status_teto_cmed, teto_cmed_unitario_pb_min tmin, teto_cmed_unitario_pb_max tmax, alerta_estimativa_acima_teto_cmed alerta FROM itens ORDER BY v DESC LIMIT 40")
s("SELECT item, descricao FROM itens WHERE lower(descricao) LIKE '%insulin%'")
s("SELECT DISTINCT base_disponibilidade, data_disponibilidade FROM itens")
EOF

"""Exploração da tabela itens: status, valores, distribuição (diagnóstico)."""
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "scripts"); import consulta_agente as q
import pandas as pd
pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 60); pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 80)
con = q.conectar()
s = lambda sql: print(con.execute(sql).df().to_string(), "\n")
s("SELECT count(*) n, sum(valor_total_estimado_orgao) v, sum(quantidade_estimada*preco_unitario_estimado_orgao) v2 FROM itens")
for c in ["status_necessidade","status_identificacao","status_preco_praticado","status_teto_cmed","catmat_status","cmed_melhor_classe","fonte","classe_temporal","unidade"]:
    s(f"SELECT {c}, count(*) n, round(sum(valor_total_estimado_orgao),2) valor, round(100*sum(valor_total_estimado_orgao)/4952438,2) pct FROM itens GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC")
s("SELECT alerta_estimativa_acima_teto_cmed, count(*) n, round(sum(valor_total_estimado_orgao),2) v FROM itens GROUP BY 1")
s("SELECT inconsistencia_unidade, count(*) n, round(sum(valor_total_estimado_orgao),2) v FROM itens GROUP BY 1")
s("SELECT cmed_alguma_com_cap, count(*) n, round(sum(valor_total_estimado_orgao),2) v FROM itens GROUP BY 1")
s("SELECT fontes_preco_praticado, count(*) n FROM itens GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC")
s("SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE qtd_licitada_pregoes_proprios_2024>0) n_lic, sum(valor_total_estimado_orgao) FILTER (WHERE qtd_licitada_pregoes_proprios_2024>0) v FROM itens")
s("SELECT item, descricao, unidade, quantidade_estimada q, preco_unitario_estimado_orgao p, valor_total_estimado_orgao v, status_preco_praticado, status_teto_cmed, teto_cmed_unitario_pb_min tmin, teto_cmed_unitario_pb_max tmax, alerta_estimativa_acima_teto_cmed alerta FROM itens ORDER BY v DESC LIMIT 40")
s("SELECT item, descricao FROM itens WHERE lower(descricao) LIKE '%insulin%'")
s("SELECT DISTINCT base_disponibilidade, data_disponibilidade FROM itens")
EOF
python -I -X utf8 trabalho/01_explora_itens.py > trabalho/01_explora_itens.txt 2>&1; cat trabalho/01_explora_itens.txt

"""Exploração das fontes de preço praticado, CMED (tipo_produto, CAP, alíquota) e PNCP para definir a metodologia de referência."""
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "scripts"); import consulta_agente as q
import pandas as pd
pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 60); pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 90)
con = q.conectar()
s = lambda sql: print(con.execute(sql).df().to_string(), "\n")
s("SELECT year(data_compra) a, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT item) itens, sum(flag_preco_extremo::int) ext, sum(flag_duplicata_negocio::int) dup FROM v_bps_comparavel GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1")
s("SELECT year(data_compra) a, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT item) itens, sum(flag_possivel_duplicata_bps::int) dup, max(data_resultado) dr FROM v_comprasgov_comparavel GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1")
s("SELECT esfera, count(*) FROM v_comprasgov_comparavel GROUP BY 1")
s("SELECT esfera, count(*) FROM v_bps_comparavel GROUP BY 1")
s("SELECT regiao, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT item) FROM v_bps_comparavel GROUP BY 1")
s("SELECT DISTINCT categoria_valor FROM v_bps_comparavel UNION ALL SELECT DISTINCT categoria_valor FROM v_comprasgov_comparavel UNION ALL SELECT DISTINCT categoria_valor FROM pncp_itens UNION ALL SELECT DISTINCT categoria_valor FROM pncp_resultados UNION ALL SELECT DISTINCT categoria_valor FROM cmed_precos")
s("SELECT tipo_produto, count(*) FROM cmed_apresentacoes GROUP BY 1")
s("SELECT regime_preco, count(*) FROM cmed_apresentacoes GROUP BY 1")
s("SELECT aplicabilidade, tipo_preco, aliquota_aplicavel_pb, count(*) FROM cmed_precos GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 4 DESC LIMIT 20")
s("SELECT item_status, count(*) FROM (SELECT item, CASE WHEN count(*) FILTER (WHERE data_compra >= '2023-01-29')>=5 THEN 'recente>=5' WHEN count(*)>=5 THEN 'total>=5' WHEN count(*)>0 THEN '1-4' ELSE '0' END item_status FROM (SELECT item, data_compra FROM v_bps_comparavel WHERE NOT flag_preco_extremo AND NOT flag_duplicata_negocio UNION ALL SELECT item, data_compra FROM v_comprasgov_comparavel WHERE NOT flag_possivel_duplicata_bps) GROUP BY item) GROUP BY 1")
s("SELECT status_preco_praticado, count(*) n, sum(bps_registros_compativeis) b, sum(comprasgov_registros_compativeis) c, sum(bps_registros_a_conferir) ba, sum(comprasgov_registros_a_conferir) ca, sum(pncp_resultados_disponiveis) pr, sum(pncp_itens_com_preco_estimado) pe FROM itens GROUP BY 1")
s("SELECT compatibilidade, count(*), count(DISTINCT item) FROM item_comprasgov GROUP BY 1")
s("SELECT compatibilidade, count(*), count(DISTINCT item) FROM item_bps_grupos GROUP BY 1")

"""Insulinas em caneta: registros BPS/Compras.gov.br dos CATMAT 440255, 442012, 468664 (e vínculo aos itens 194/195); vínculo com ERRO da inspeção IA."""
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "scripts"); import consulta_agente as q
import pandas as pd
pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 60); pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 70)
con = q.conectar()
s = lambda sql: print(con.execute(sql).df().to_string(), "\n")
s("SELECT item, catmat, descricao_catmat, nivel, criterio FROM item_catmat WHERE item BETWEEN 194 AND 199")
s("SELECT catmat, descricao_catmat, unidade_fornecimento, capacidade_descricao, uf, esfera, data_compra, quantidade, preco_unitario_praticado, flag_preco_extremo, flag_duplicata_negocio FROM bps WHERE catmat IN ('440255','442012','468664') ORDER BY catmat, data_compra")
s("SELECT catmat, descricao_detalhada, unidade_fornecimento, capacidade_valor, marca, uf, esfera, data_compra, quantidade, preco_unitario_praticado, flag_possivel_duplicata_bps FROM comprasgov WHERE catmat IN ('440255','442012','468664') ORDER BY catmat, data_compra")
s("SELECT r.item, r.catmat, r.compatibilidade, count(*) FROM item_comprasgov r WHERE item BETWEEN 194 AND 199 GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1")
s("SELECT item, registro, apresentacao, fator_conversao, teto_unitario_pb, inspecao_amostral_ia, status FROM regras_conversao WHERE inspecao_amostral_ia LIKE 'ERRO%' OR inspecao_amostral_ia LIKE '%RESSALVA%'")
EOF
python -I -X utf8 trabalho/05_insulinas_catmat.py > trabalho/05_insulinas_catmat.txt 2>&1; cat trabalho/05_insulinas_catmat.txt
input.description: Inspect insulin pen CATMAT records and flagged conversions

"""Confere como o pacote calcula teto_cmed_unitario_pb_min/max e quantos tetos dependem de vínculos COM ALERTA."""
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "scripts"); import consulta_agente as q
import pandas as pd
pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 60); pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 80)
con = q.conectar()
s = lambda sql: print(con.execute(sql).df().to_string(), "\n")
base = """WITH t AS (SELECT t.*, r.status, r.inspecao_amostral_ia FROM v_cmed_teto_unitario t JOIN regras_conversao r ON r.item=t.item AND CAST(r.registro AS VARCHAR)=t.registro
      WHERE t.aliquota_aplicavel_pb AND t.aplicabilidade IN ('teto para compras administrativas','teto obrigatório (produto com CAP)'))"""
s(base + """, a AS (SELECT item, min(valor_por_unidade_item) mn_all, max(valor_por_unidade_item) mx_all,
      min(valor_por_unidade_item) FILTER (WHERE status NOT LIKE '%COM ALERTA%' AND coalesce(inspecao_amostral_ia,'') NOT LIKE 'ERRO%') mn_ok,
      max(valor_por_unidade_item) FILTER (WHERE status NOT LIKE '%COM ALERTA%' AND coalesce(inspecao_amostral_ia,'') NOT LIKE 'ERRO%') mx_ok, count(*) n FROM t GROUP BY item)
    SELECT count(*) itens, count(*) FILTER (WHERE abs(mn_all - i.teto_cmed_unitario_pb_min)<1e-6 AND abs(mx_all-i.teto_cmed_unitario_pb_max)<1e-6) iguais_pacote,
      count(*) FILTER (WHERE mx_ok IS NULL) so_alerta, count(*) FILTER (WHERE mx_ok <> mx_all OR mn_ok <> mn_all) muda_com_alerta
    FROM a JOIN itens i USING (item)""")
s(base + """ SELECT item, registro, apresentacao, fator_conversao, tipo_preco, valor_embalagem, valor_por_unidade_item, status FROM t WHERE status LIKE '%COM ALERTA%' AND item IN (SELECT item FROM itens WHERE alerta_estimativa_acima_teto_cmed) ORDER BY item LIMIT 60""")
s("SELECT count(*) n, count(*) FILTER (WHERE teto_cmed_unitario_pb_max IS NOT NULL) com_teto FROM itens")
EOF

DESC = {"Genérico": 0.6011, "Similar": 0.5101}  # demais tipos: 0.1801 (éticos)

itens = df("SELECT * FROM itens ORDER BY item")

prat = df(f"""
SELECT item, 'BPS' fonte, catmat, uf, esfera, data_compra, preco_unitario_praticado p FROM v_bps_comparavel
 WHERE NOT coalesce(flag_preco_extremo,false) AND NOT coalesce(flag_duplicata_negocio,false) AND preco_unitario_praticado > 0
UNION ALL
SELECT item, 'Compras.gov.br', catmat, uf, esfera, data_compra, preco_unitario_praticado FROM v_comprasgov_comparavel
 WHERE NOT coalesce(flag_possivel_duplicata_bps,false) AND preco_unitario_praticado > 0""")
for it, cm in CATMAT_ESPECIFICO.items():
    prat = prat[(prat.item != it) | (prat.catmat == cm)]
prat["recente"] = prat.data_compra >= pd.Timestamp(JANELA)

def resumo(g, pref):
    rec = g[g.recente]
    use, jan = (rec, "24m") if len(rec) >= 5 else (g, "total")
    p = use.p
    return pd.Series({f"{pref}_n": len(use), f"{pref}_n_total": len(g), f"{pref}_janela": jan, f"{pref}_ufs": use.uf.nunique(),
                      f"{pref}_p25": p.quantile(.25), f"{pref}_med": p.median(), f"{pref}_p75": p.quantile(.75),
                      f"{pref}_fontes": "|".join(sorted(use.fonte.unique())),
                      f"{pref}_med_municipal": use.loc[use.esfera.isin(["M", "MUNICIPAL"]), "p"].median()})

SELECT item, 'BPS' fonte, uf, esfera, data_compra, preco_unitario_praticado p, compatibilidade FROM v_bps_a_conferir
 WHERE NOT coalesce(flag_preco_extremo,false) AND NOT coalesce(flag_duplicata_negocio,false) AND preco_unitario_praticado > 0
UNION ALL
SELECT item, 'Compras.gov.br', uf, esfera, data_compra, preco_unitario_praticado, compatibilidade FROM v_comprasgov_a_conferir
 WHERE NOT coalesce(flag_possivel_duplicata_bps,false) AND preco_unitario_praticado > 0""")
conf["recente"] = conf.data_compra >= pd.Timestamp(JANELA)
rc = conf.groupby("item").apply(lambda g: resumo(g, "conf"), include_groups=False).reset_index()
rc = rc[["item", "conf_n", "conf_janela", "conf_p25", "conf_med", "conf_p75"]]
rc_tipo = conf.groupby("item").compatibilidade.agg(lambda s: "|".join(sorted(set(s)))).rename("conf_motivos").reset_index()

pn = df("""SELECT item,
  count(preco_unitario_homologado) pncp_n_hom, median(preco_unitario_homologado) pncp_med_hom,

  FROM v_pncp_comparavel GROUP BY item""")

teto = df("""
WITH t AS (
 SELECT t.item, t.registro, t.tipo_preco, t.aliquota_icms, t.valor_por_unidade_item teto_u, t.fator_conversao, a.tipo_produto, a.cap,
        r.status, coalesce(r.inspecao_amostral_ia,'') insp
 FROM v_cmed_teto_unitario t
 JOIN regras_conversao r ON r.item = t.item AND CAST(r.registro AS VARCHAR) = t.registro
 JOIN cmed_apresentacoes a ON a.registro = t.registro
 WHERE t.aliquota_aplicavel_pb AND t.aplicabilidade IN ('teto para compras administrativas','teto obrigatório (produto com CAP)')),
pf AS (SELECT item, registro, valor_por_unidade_item pf_u FROM v_cmed_teto_unitario WHERE aliquota_aplicavel_pb AND tipo_preco = 'PF'),
a20 AS (SELECT item, registro, tipo_preco, valor_por_unidade_item teto20_u FROM v_cmed_teto_unitario WHERE aliquota_icms = '20%')
SELECT t.*, pf.pf_u, a20.teto20_u,
       (t.status NOT LIKE '%COM ALERTA%' AND t.insp NOT LIKE 'ERRO%') ok
FROM t JOIN pf USING (item, registro) LEFT JOIN a20 USING (item, registro, tipo_preco)""")
teto["desc"] = teto.tipo_produto.map(DESC).fillna(D_ETICO)
teto["e2_u"] = np.minimum(teto.pf_u * (1 - teto.desc), teto.teto_u)  # desconto sobre PF, limitado ao teto (PMVG se CAP)
ok = teto[teto.ok]
rt = ok.groupby("item").agg(teto_min=("teto_u", "min"), teto_max=("teto_u", "max"), teto_n=("registro", "nunique"),
                            teto_tipos=("tipo_preco", lambda s: "|".join(sorted(set(s)))),
                            teto_aliq=("aliquota_icms", lambda s: "|".join(sorted(set(s)))),
                            teto_max_aliq20=("teto20_u", "max"), cap_algum=("cap", "max"),
                            e2_min=("e2_u", "min"), e2_med=("e2_u", "median"), e2_max=("e2_u", "max"),
                            tipos_produto=("tipo_produto", lambda s: "|".join(sorted(set(s))))).reset_index()
rt_all = teto.groupby("item").agg(teto_max_todos=("teto_u", "max"), n_vinc_alerta=("ok", lambda s: int((~s).sum()))).reset_index()

r = (itens[["item", "descricao", "unidade", "quantidade_estimada", "preco_unitario_estimado_orgao", "valor_total_estimado_orgao",
            "status_identificacao", "status_preco_praticado", "status_teto_cmed", "cmed_melhor_classe", "teto_cmed_unitario_pb_min",
            "teto_cmed_unitario_pb_max", "alerta_estimativa_acima_teto_cmed", "inconsistencia_unidade", "qtd_licitada_pregoes_proprios_2024"]]
     .merge(rp, on="item", how="left").merge(rc, on="item", how="left").merge(rc_tipo, on="item", how="left")
     .merge(pn, on="item", how="left").merge(rt, on="item", how="left").merge(rt_all, on="item", how="left"))
r = r.rename(columns={"quantidade_estimada": "q", "preco_unitario_estimado_orgao": "p_org", "valor_total_estimado_orgao": "v_org"})

# dispersão empírica (para referências pontuais): mediana entre itens com >=5 preços de p25/med e p75/med
base = r[(r.prat_n >= 5) & (r.prat_med > 0)]
K_LOW = float((base.prat_p25 / base.prat_med).median())
K_HIGH = float((base.prat_p75 / base.prat_med).median())

cap = lambda v, t: v if pd.isna(t) else min(v, t)

def referencia(x):
    """Preço de referência E1 (central, baixo, alto), fonte e categoria_valor."""
    t = x.teto_max
    if x.prat_n >= 1 if not pd.isna(x.prat_n) else False:
        c, lo, hi = x.prat_med, x.prat_p25, x.prat_p75
        fonte = f"praticado compatível ({x.prat_fontes}; janela {x.prat_janela}; n={int(x.prat_n)})"
        cat = "preco_unitario_praticado_por_unidade_fornecimento (mediana)"
    elif x.pncp_n_hom >= 1 if not pd.isna(x.pncp_n_hom) else False:
        c = x.pncp_med_hom; lo, hi = c * K_LOW, c * K_HIGH
        fonte = f"PNCP homologado por outro órgão (n={int(x.pncp_n_hom)})"; cat = "preco_unitario_homologado (por unidade do item)"
    elif x.pncp_n_est >= 1 if not pd.isna(x.pncp_n_est) else False:
        c = x.pncp_med_est; lo, hi = c * K_LOW, c * K_HIGH
        fonte = f"PNCP estimado por outro órgão (n={int(x.pncp_n_est)})"; cat = "preco_unitario_estimado_por_outro_orgao (por unidade do item)"
    elif not pd.isna(x.e2_med):
        c, lo, hi = x.e2_med, x.e2_min, x.e2_max
        fonte = "teto CMED PB × (1 − desconto PE 12/2024 por tipo de produto)"; cat = "derivado: limite_regulatorio × (1 − desconto obtido em 2024)"
    else:
        c = x.p_org; lo, hi = c * K_LOW, c
        fonte = "estimativa do órgão (sem referência externa utilizável)"; cat = "preco_estimado_pelo_orgao"
    teto_bind = (not pd.isna(t)) and c > t
    return pd.Series({"p_ref": cap(c, t), "p_low": min(cap(lo, t), cap(c, t)), "p_high": max(cap(hi, t), cap(c, t)),
                      "fonte_ref": fonte + (" — limitado ao teto CMED" if teto_bind else ""), "categoria_valor_ref": cat,
                      "ref_limitada_teto": teto_bind})

r = pd.concat([r, r.apply(referencia, axis=1)], axis=1)

# cenário "a conferir compatível": usa mediana a conferir (limitada ao teto) no lugar do central
r["p_se_conferir_compativel"] = [cap(m, t) if not pd.isna(m) else np.nan for m, t in zip(r.conf_med, r.teto_max)]
r["flag_a_conferir"] = r.status_preco_praticado.eq("a conferir")
r["flag_acima_teto_pacote"] = r.alerta_estimativa_acima_teto_cmed.fillna(False)

r["flag_sem_referencia_externa"] = r.fonte_ref.str.startswith("estimativa do órgão")
r["flag_sem_teto_utilizavel"] = r.teto_max.isna()
r["flag_ref_fraca"] = ~(r.prat_n >= 5)
r["p_org_limitado_teto"] = [cap(p, t) for p, t in zip(r.p_org, r.teto_max)]

r.to_csv("trabalho/ref_itens.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8")

# ---------- auto-verificação ----------
assert len(r) == 334 and r.item.is_unique

assert (r.p_low <= r.p_ref + 1e-9).all() and (r.p_ref <= r.p_high + 1e-9).all()
assert (r.teto_max.isna() | (r.p_ref <= r.teto_max + 1e-9)).all()
assert not r.p_ref.isna().any()

with open("trabalho/10_referencias.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    w = lambda *a: print(*a, file=f)
    w(f"K_LOW={K_LOW:.4f} K_HIGH={K_HIGH:.4f} (n itens base={len(base)})")
    w(r.groupby(r.fonte_ref.str.split(" \\(| —").str[0]).agg(n=("item", "size"), v_org=("v_org", "sum"),
      v_ref=("p_ref", lambda s: (s * r.loc[s.index, "q"]).sum())).to_string())
    w("itens com teto confirmado:", int((~r.teto_max.isna()).sum()), "| com teto (todos os vínculos) no pacote:", int((~r.teto_cmed_unitario_pb_max.isna()).sum()))
    w("ref limitada ao teto:", int(r.ref_limitada_teto.sum()))
    w("acima teto pacote:", int(r.flag_acima_teto_pacote.sum()), round(r.loc[r.flag_acima_teto_pacote, "v_org"].sum(), 2),
      "| acima teto confirmado:", int(r.flag_acima_teto_confirmado.sum()), round(r.loc[r.flag_acima_teto_confirmado, "v_org"].sum(), 2))
    w("a conferir:", int(r.flag_a_conferir.sum()), round(r.loc[r.flag_a_conferir, "v_org"].sum(), 2))
    w("sem referência externa:", int(r.flag_sem_referencia_externa.sum()), round(r.loc[r.flag_sem_referencia_externa, "v_org"].sum(), 2))

    m = r.prat_med_municipal.notna() & r.prat_med.gt(0)
    w(f"razão mediana municipal/mediana geral (itens com ambos): mediana={float((r.prat_med_municipal[m]/r.prat_med[m]).median()):.4f} "
      f"p25={float((r.prat_med_municipal[m]/r.prat_med[m]).quantile(.25)):.4f} p75={float((r.prat_med_municipal[m]/r.prat_med[m]).quantile(.75)):.4f}")
print(open("trabalho/10_referencias.txt", encoding="utf-8").read())
